questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?

options.text: 3 psi in one minute
6 psi in one minute
8 psi in one minute
4 psi in one minute

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because it needs repairs.

questions.question: How do states make sure drivers only have one license?

options.text: You will sign a form
States share driver information in a computer database
Your wallet will be searched

questions.correctAnswerText: States share driver information in a computer database
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have more than one driver license. All states share driver information in a computer database to prevent giving licenses to drivers who already have one.

questions.question: If another vehicle pulls out in front of you and you cannot stop, what should you do?

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it will be their fault
Swerve to avoid the other car
Put your vehicle in reverse
Speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve to avoid the other car
questions.explanation: If another vehicle pulls out in front of you, brake if you have room to stop. If you don't have room to stop, swerving is the safer choice.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A person talking to another person in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Watch out for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers. A person sitting on a bench is not a safety concern.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:

options.text: Low centers of gravity
High centers of gravity
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: High centers of gravity
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load weight can shift while driving.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be placed:

options.text: As high as possible
As low as possible
As far to the left as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Weight should be placed as low as possible to keep the vehicle stable.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a serious traffic violation?

options.text: Excessive speeding
Littering
Reckless driving
Following too closely

questions.correctAnswerText: Littering
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include excessive speeding, reckless driving, operating a commercial vehicle without a valid license, following too closely, and improper lane use. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your license. Littering is not a serious traffic violation.

questions.question: When an oncoming vehicle at night has bright headlights, how can you avoid being blinded?

options.text: Wear sunglasses
Close your eyes
Glance to the side of the road
Use your high beams

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance to the side of the road
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by an oncoming vehicle's bright lights at night, glance to the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: During the driving test at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train
Not change gears while on the tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where is the ABS malfunction lamp located?

options.text: On the driver's door
On the instrument panel
On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door
Under the hood

questions.correctAnswerText: On the instrument panel
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have a yellow malfunction lamp on the instrument panel. Trailers have a yellow ABS lamp on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: When checking tire condition during the vehicle inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the inside of the tires are more worn than the outside.
Make sure the outside of the tires are more worn than the inside.
Make sure the middle of the tires are more worn than the outside.
Make sure the tires wear evenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the tires wear evenly.
questions.explanation: When you check your tires during the vehicle inspection, the tread should wear evenly across the tire.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, your best option to stop is:

options.text: An escape ramp.
Drive on the shoulder.
Stay on the road.
Hit a slower vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: An escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, use an escape ramp if available. If no escape ramp exists, look for another way out, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To protect the cargo from animals

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals
questions.explanation: You should cover cargo to protect people from spills and to protect the cargo from weather. Protecting cargo from animals is not a main reason to cover cargo.

questions.question: A cargo of hanging meat:

options.text: Is stable because of how it is loaded.
Can be a problem because animals may be attracted to the meat.
Is unstable because it has a high center of gravity.
Should not be transported in summer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is unstable because it has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity. The meat also swings when the vehicle moves, which makes it harder to control the vehicle. You must drive carefully when transporting this type of load.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:

options.text: Once a week.
Once a month.
After every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: You must complete an after-trip inspection at the end of every trip, day, or duty period. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its load
The total weight of a vehicle's tractor
The total weight of a loaded trailer
The weight of a tractor and trailer before loading

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its load
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus everything it is carrying.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: For the CDL vehicle inspection test, you will walk around the vehicle, point to or touch items, and explain what you are checking and why. You will not need to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers. A person waiting on a bench is not a distraction concern.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce normal braking power.
Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
Do not work well on larger vehicles.
Are illegal in some states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with the vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?

options.text: Color
Length
Weight
Number of windows

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A light load makes it sit higher. If your vehicle fits under a bridge when fully loaded, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Inspect the cargo only if it is making noise.
Inspect the cargo only if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo and how it is secured before you start driving. Then check it again within the first 50 miles. After that, check every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: In a vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: Looking at the gauges on your dashboard.
Checking your blind spots.
Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check where it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check where it is.
questions.explanation: A look means you open your door, get out, and walk to the back of your vehicle to see where it is. During straight line backing, you can only do one look. During other exercises, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: What is controlled braking?

options.text: Locking the wheels while steering.
Pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
Lightly tapping the brakes.
Downshifting gears to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means you press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while using controlled braking, release the brake, turn the wheel, then apply the brakes again.

questions.question: What must you do if a load is too long?

options.text: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
Transport it only between 6 p.m. and 3 a.m.
Shorten the load.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put a warning flag on the end of the load.
questions.explanation: For an over-length load, you may need warning flags or flashing lights. You will also need a permit. Driving times are often limited.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing has no warning gates or lights, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because the tracks are probably not in use.
Park and walk to the tracks to see if a train is coming.
Look both directions down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
Do what other drivers around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both directions down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look both ways down the tracks to check for trains.

questions.question: How should cargo be secured on flatbed trailers?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers or trailers without walls must be tied down so it does not move or fall during transport.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly.
Check the load and how it is secured after driving no more than 50 miles.
Do not use your mirrors to look behind.
Hold your cell phone in case of an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and how it is secured after driving no more than 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo and its securing devices before you start driving. Then check again within the first 50 miles. After that, check every three hours or every 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: To know if your vehicle can handle a load, you need to know:

options.text: Your vehicle's suspension rating.
The rating of your front tires only.
The rating of your rear tires only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: It is your job to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. You must know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can safely carry, including the suspension system's weight rating.

questions.question: What should you do with manual air tank drains?

options.text: Open them to drain the tanks at the end of each day.
Leave them open while driving.
Seal them with glue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open them to drain the tanks at the end of each day.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in the brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you not do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Spray foam through the louvers.
Open the hood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the hood.
questions.explanation: If your engine is on fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can avoid it.

questions.question: What skill must you be able to do on a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Back into an alley.
Weave between cones.
Make an emergency stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back into an alley.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include: straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley backing.

questions.question: When the drive wheels skid while braking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle goes straight again.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid: First, release the brake pedal so the locked wheels can roll again. Steer quickly in the direction you want to go. Then countersteer to prevent the vehicle from skidding the other way.

questions.question: What can happen if brakes overheat while going downhill?

options.text: They become sticky.
They stop working.
They squeak.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop working.
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes can cause them to overheat. When this happens, they lose their stopping power. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: What condition may be needed when checking an automatic transmission fluid?

options.text: The vehicle parked on a slope upward.
The vehicle parked on a slope downward.
The engine running.
The vehicle lifted with a jack.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine running.
questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Why should tires be checked regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.
The tread wears down much faster.
The lug nuts may become loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands. In very hot weather, tire air pressure can reach dangerous levels. If this happens, stop and let the tires cool. Do not let air out, because pressure will drop too much when the tires cool down.

questions.question: What should a driver do when carrying a sealed load?

options.text: Inspect what is inside.
Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed weight limits.
Open each container to check it.
Unseal the load to check it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed weight limits.
questions.explanation: A driver cannot open sealed loads. However, they must ensure the total weight and axle weight do not exceed legal limits.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does the absence of spray from other vehicles mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The pavement is dry.
Spray is stuck under the vehicles.
The tires have absorbed all moisture.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicle tires are not creating spray, ice has formed on the road. Drive very carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Why is rolling backward when you start to move forward dangerous?

options.text: It may damage the transmission.
Trucks cannot go backward.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can move forward without rolling backward first. Rolling backward can cause you to hit a vehicle or object behind your truck.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether the road is becoming icy, what can you do?

options.text: Guess.
Open your window and feel the front of the side mirror for ice.
Look at the road closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the front of the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road might be getting icy, open your window and touch the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on any of these, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering system, what must you check?

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses contain no fluid.
Only small leaks are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks and fix them before driving.

questions.question: The examiner will score you on what during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How quickly you reach your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, follow all laws, and avoid accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Stay on.
Flash on and off.
Turn off immediately.
Turn off once you start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off immediately.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after the engine starts. This includes the charging light, oil light, coolant light, and ABS light.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, you should check that:

options.text: The vehicle looks shinier than others.
The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
The vehicle is parked correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: Check the vehicle's general condition before an inspection. Look for damage or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Check for hazards around the vehicle, such as people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: ABS cannot work because of weather.
ABS has just been activated.
ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light means something in the anti-lock braking system is not working correctly.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Make gestures at other drivers.
Assume other drivers have good reasons for what they do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for what they do.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, give other drivers the benefit of the doubt. Assume they have valid reasons for their actions and do not take it personally.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Pushes the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Pushes the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after driving for a bit to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Repair the brakes.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.
Add more air to the tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop after driving for a bit to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, drive for a while, then stop and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: If a worker is in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
Drive on the grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, follow the posted speed limits. If workers are present, drive even slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: In cold weather, an alcohol evaporator should be checked and filled:

options.text: Once a week.
Every day.
Every hour.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in air brakes. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are not safe to use.
Are acceptable on combination vehicles.
Are acceptable only when driving under 40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.
